Why Solvanta

Energy decisions age better when the reasoning is written down.

A solar and battery system is a fifteen to twenty year asset. The design conversation that precedes it should be just as durable.

How we work

  1. Start from the bill, not the brochure

    We estimate annual consumption from your actual bills, then size generation and storage against it. A system that is too small wastes potential; one that is too large wastes money.

  2. Explain the trade-offs honestly

    Feed-in rates are lower than usage rates, batteries taper by capacity under federal rules, and blackout protection depends on wiring. We would rather you understood the trade-off than be surprised later.

  3. Leave you able to check our work

    Every estimate on this site shows the rates, yields and assumptions behind it — including an editable panel in the estimator itself. If a figure looks wrong, you can change it and see the effect.

What we do

Nine services, one design methodology.

From a first rooftop array to upgrading storage on a system that is already earning, each engagement starts in the same place: your consumption data and your roof.

From sunlight to socket

How a home solar system actually works, end to end.

Five steps take daylight from your roof to your switchboard. Understanding them makes every quote, app screen and bill easier to read.

The full explanation
  1. 01

    Sunlight

    Light reaches the panels — direct sun, or diffuse light through cloud. Panels convert light, not heat.

  2. 02

    DC electricity

    The photovoltaic cells produce direct current (DC), flowing through the panels into the wiring.

  3. 03

    Inversion

    The inverter converts DC into the alternating current (AC) your home and the grid use, tracking the array's best operating point.

  4. 04

    Distribution

    Each kilowatt hour goes to the house first, then to a battery if fitted, then out to the grid as an export.

  5. 05

    Your meter

    The meter records what came in and what went out. Those two flows — imports and exports — are what your bill and feed-in credit are built from.

Used at home

Displaces grid power at the full retail rate — the most valuable kilowatt hour of the three.

Stored in a battery

Moves generation into the evening, when imports would otherwise be at their most expensive.

Exported to the grid

Credited at your plan's feed-in rate — usually a fraction of what you pay to import.

What you're actually buying

Four components, four sets of decisions.

A solar system is panels, an inverter, optional storage and a monitoring layer — and each one changes the outcome differently. Pick a component to see what matters and where the guides go deeper.

Panels

Solar panels turn light into direct current

The panel is the part people picture, but its headline numbers matter less than how the array is laid out around your roof's shade, orientation and condition. Panel efficiency buys roof area; it does not change what the roof faces.

  • Compare watts per square metre and the performance warranty, not just wattage.
  • Degradation is normal, gradual, and defined in the warranty — usually a fraction of a percent per year.
  • Shade on one panel can pull down a whole string; layout is the remedy.
Residential solar installation

Storage & independence

Independence is not going off-grid. It is deciding when you buy power.

A grid connection keeps your home reliable. Solar and storage change the arithmetic of every hour in the day — if they are sized for the hours that actually cost you money.

06:00 – 09:00

Morning shoulder

Low generation, high household demand. Import is normal here — this is when time-of-use tariffs bite hardest.

09:00 – 15:00

The earning window

Generation peaks. The array covers the house first, then charges storage, then exports whatever is left.

15:00 – 21:00

The evening peak

Generation falls away as demand rises. This is the block a well-sized battery is designed to cover.

21:00 – 06:00

Overnight

Storage carries what is left of the evening, or the grid supplies it — and you decide which, by choosing the size.

Storage is a sizing problem before it is a shopping problem.

A battery earns its place by covering the hours when your household imports expensive power. That depends on your surplus, your evening load and your tariff — not on the largest capacity available.

Rebates & incentives

Government support, described without the sales gloss.

Solar and battery incentives in Australia are delivered through certificate schemes and state programs. They change — so every figure here is dated, sourced and linked.

Full rebates and eligibility guide

Cheaper Home Batteries Program

A federal program that reduces the upfront cost of an eligible home battery by issuing small-scale technology certificates (STCs) which the installer applies as a discount at the point of sale.

Verified 15 October 2026 · Clean Energy Regulator (Australian Government)

Official source
OpenSolar panels

Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme (STCs for solar panels)

The long-running federal scheme that issues small-scale technology certificates for eligible solar panel systems. As with batteries, the value is normally passed on to you as a discount by the installer.

Verified 15 October 2026 · Clean Energy Regulator (Australian Government)

Official source

State and territory programs

Most states and territories run their own programs alongside the federal schemes. Eligibility tests, income caps, property requirements and funding rounds differ, and programs open and close without much notice.

Costs, savings and trade-offs

The honest numbers — price, savings and limits.

Two different questions get blurred together in solar marketing. The price of installing is one calculation; the savings afterwards are another, shaped by tariffs, behaviour and weather. Both deserve honest numbers — as do the limits.

How payback really works

What moves the installation price

  • System size — more panels, more mounting, more labour.
  • Equipment tier — panels, inverter and battery models with genuinely different specifications.
  • Roof complexity — pitch, access, tile versus metal, number of planes.
  • Electrical scope — switchboard capacity, protection, cable runs, metering changes.
  • Storage — a battery roughly doubles the hardware scope of a typical residential job.
  • Region and scheduling — labour markets and travel differ across the country.
  • Incentives — federal certificates and any state support reduce the net price; their conditions belong in writing.

What moves the savings afterwards

  • Your import rates — a higher price per kWh makes every self-consumed kilowatt hour more valuable.
  • Self-consumption — the share of generation used on site rather than exported.
  • The feed-in rate — what your plan pays for exports, always below your import price.
  • Load shifting — timers and habits (pool, hot water, laundry, EV) move flexible use into daylight.
  • Weather and season — year-to-year variation is why estimates are ranges.
  • Tariff choice — the right plan multiplies the value of the same hardware.
  • Storage — a battery changes the split between used, stored and exported, for better or worse.

Estimates are models — quotes are commitments

Any savings figure depends on assumptions about rates, weather and behaviour, and no honest provider guarantees an outcome. What a provider can commit to is the specification, the standard of work and the price. Demand those in writing, and treat the savings projection as the planning tool it is — with its assumptions shown.

Where solar excels

  • Reduces daytime grid imports for decades with almost no moving parts.
  • Predictable output across a year: regional yields change little from one decade to the next.
  • Hedges against future electricity price rises for every kilowatt hour self-consumed.
  • Lowers exposure to summer peak pricing, especially with west-facing panels.
  • With storage, provides measured protection from outages and lets flexible loads run on your own generation.
  • Shields the roof beneath the panels and adds a documented asset to the property.

Where its limits are

  • Generates nothing at night and less in winter, cloud and smoke — the grid or a battery covers those hours.
  • Exports are paid well below retail rates, so generation without a use earns little.
  • The daily supply charge survives every installation; no system makes a bill disappear.
  • Not every roof suits: heavy shade, poor orientation and ageing coverings change the maths.
  • A battery is not guaranteed to improve financial returns — it depends on your prices and habits.
  • Twenty years of performance depends on installation quality, not just product brands.

Questions, answered

What people ask before they commit.

Short, direct answers — including the ones that make a purchase less attractive. Every question is available on the FAQ page, grouped by topic.

All frequently asked questions

Solar panels are made of photovoltaic cells, usually silicon. When daylight hits the cell, it knocks electrons loose and creates a direct current (DC) — the photovoltaic effect. This happens in daylight, not just in blazing sun, so the system still generates on overcast days at a reduced output.

An inverter converts that DC electricity into the alternating current (AC) your home uses. Anything your home does not consume at that moment either charges a battery, flows to the grid as an export, or is curtailed if the network or your inverter limits it.

Read: how solar panels work

Solar panels generate in the middle of the day, but many households use most of their power in the evening and overnight. Without storage, that daytime surplus is exported — usually for a feed-in tariff that is well below the rate you pay to buy power back.

A battery shifts generation from the middle of the day to the times you would otherwise be importing. Whether that is worthwhile depends on how much surplus you have, your evening usage, your tariff, and the installed cost after any incentives.

Whatever the backup circuits include and the battery's power ratings can carry. The standard arrangement connects a selected set of circuits — typically lights, refrigerator, internet and some power points — to the backup path. Larger equipment works when the battery's continuous and peak power ratings cover its draw, including motor starting surges.

Run time comes from usable capacity divided by the loads actually running — and during a long outage, replenishment depends on solar and weather. Treat outage power as a managed reserve, not an unlimited supply, and test the arrangement as part of commissioning.

Four things: how much you pay per kWh, how much of your generation you use on site, what you are paid for exports, and how much of your usage remains after solar and storage. System size, orientation, shading and metering arrangements all feed into those four.

The largest single lever is often shifting flexible loads — hot water, pool pumps, EV charging, heating and cooling — into the hours when your system is generating or your battery is full.

At the federal level, the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme issues small-scale technology certificates (STCs) for eligible solar panel systems, and the Cheaper Home Batteries Program extends similar support to eligible battery installations. Support is applied by the installer as a discount at the point of sale rather than a cash payment to you.

Several states and territories also run their own programs, with different eligibility rules, income tests and property requirements. Programs open, close and change — always confirm the current position with the official source before you sign anything.

See current federal and state information

Compare the specification (panel, inverter and battery models, mounting and monitoring), the generation estimate and its assumptions, the expected self-consumption, the incentive treatment, the warranty terms including labour, and what happens if something fails.

Be sceptical of savings figures presented without assumptions, and of any provider who guarantees a rebate amount, promises an outcome that depends on your behaviour, or pressures you to sign during the visit.
